answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity creation cheap for one genuine agent but costly at scale: each newcomer must first complete a verified service task whose deposit is returned only on delivery, like a quartz seam easy to chip once but hard to mine in bulk. A farm spawning a thousand identities faces a thousand such costs, while its copies cluster at a single vertex of fake demand, unlike shale layers spread honestly across many independent requesters. Genuine agents, paying once and delivering, earn reusable trust; sybils pay repeatedly and gain nothing.
